author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A new memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran may have brought an end to immediate hostilities, but major questions remain over whether it can deliver lasting peace.

Al Jazeera's senior political analyst Marwan Bishara says the agreement appears to be a broad framework rather than a detailed peace deal, allowing both sides to claim success while opening the door to further negotiations.

The deal is expected to focus on key issues including the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear programme, Lebanon and wider regional security.

While the agreement could reduce tensions and prevent a wider conflict, analysts caution that the difficult details still lie ahead and that a ceasefire does not necessarily guarantee long-term stability.

Both Washington and Tehran appear to have strong incentives to reach an agreement, but whether this diplomatic breakthrough leads to a lasting settlement remains uncertain.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump says Washington has reached an agreement with Iran and plans to issue a statement confirming the deal, though Tehran has yet to publicly confirm the announcement.

According to Trump, the agreement would include an Iranian commitment not to obtain nuclear weapons and an immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies.

The president also said sanctions on Iran could potentially be lifted, while ruling out providing Tehran with cash as part of the deal.

If signed, the memorandum of understanding would reportedly trigger a 60-day negotiation period to address the most difficult issues, including Iran's enriched uranium stockpiles and the future of its civilian nuclear programme.

Despite signs of progress, significant differences remain over the details of the agreement, with Washington and Tehran presenting differing accounts of what the deal contains.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Ukraine has launched several large scale drone attacks on Russia, with eight regions reporting strikes. An apartment block in the city of Oryol caught fire, and an oil depot in Rybinsk north of Moscow also burned, causing traffic restrictions. Marina Miron, a military analyst at King’s College London, said Ukraine has adopted what US military theorist JC Wylie called a “cumulative strategy” – attacking logistics, fuel depots and rear areas not for single decisive blows but for a cumulative effect that disrupts Russia’s war economy. While the economic impact may not be huge yet, the strikes create pressure on the Kremlin and Russia’s General Staff, which must now reallocate resources to protect facilities from drones – a task its layered air defence was not designed for.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
China has become a global leader in clean energy, driven by massive investments in solar panels and wind turbines. Now, it is betting that the future of the energy transition lies in battery storage.

Battery systems can store electricity generated by renewable sources and release it when needed, helping households, businesses and entire power grids cope with fluctuating energy demand.

The industry has grown rapidly as battery costs have fallen, with China accounting for around 60 percent of global battery storage additions last year.

Supporters say battery storage could lower electricity costs and help power energy-intensive technologies such as artificial intelligence and data centres.

But some analysts warn the sector could face challenges similar to China's solar industry, where intense competition and overcapacity have squeezed profits.

For now, China is positioning itself not only as a leader in producing clean energy, but also in storing it.

title: China Bets on Battery Storage as the Next Clean Energy Frontier

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Health workers in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are battling not only Ebola but also widespread misinformation and mistrust about the deadly virus.

In Kapanga camp, home to around 30,000 internally displaced people, aid workers are going door to door to educate residents about how Ebola spreads and how to protect themselves.

Several cases have already been recorded in the camp, with some patients dying from the disease. Health officials say skepticism remains a major obstacle, with some patients refusing treatment and others denying that Ebola exists.

The crowded conditions and poor sanitation in displacement camps have increased concerns about further transmission, while the lack of specialised treatment facilities is complicating the response.
